items.title: perf(flydsl): optimize Kimi-K3 KDA group64 projection on gfx950
items.body:
## Summary

Add a fixed-shape FlyDSL weight-only FP8 projection for the Kimi-K3 KDA input
linear on gfx950. The wrapper accepts only the exact TP8 decode contract and
fails closed for every unsupported device, shape, dtype, layout, or padding.

The BF16 checkpoint weight is quantized once into FP8 e4m3 group64 storage.
The kernel accumulates in FP32, writes BF16 output, and uses the schedule
selected by the cache-valid MI355X sweep: two rows per wave, 256 CUs, and
weight cache modifier 2. Tuning controls are intentionally not part of the
public API.

## Scope

- one gfx950 fixed-shape kernel;
- one typed wrapper and model-load quantizer;
- one focused correctness/contract test file.

No existing generic GEMM, MoE, attention, or non-gfx950 dispatch is changed.

## Correctness

The focused suite checks the exact support contract, fail-closed argument
validation, fixed launch schedule, 24 seeded random inputs, real Kimi-K3
checkpoint weights, finite output, exact zero padding, relative RMSE no greater
than `5e-4`, and cosine similarity at least `0.99999` against a
BF16-rounded reference.

```text
pytest -q op_tests/flydsl_tests/test_kimi_k3_kda_input_group64.py
11 passed in 15.15s
```

## Performance

Hardware: 1x MI355X (`gfx950`, 256 CUs). Shape: M=1, N=6,288 stored as
6,284 logical rows, K=7,168. The control is the installed vLLM BF16
`wvSplitK`; the candidate is the production wrapper in this PR. Both use the
same real checkpoint weight and eight rotating representations. Each fresh
process performs 100,000 warmup operations followed by 21 paired alternating
trials.

| Process | BF16 control p50 | Group64 p50 | Speedup | Saved per call |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 15.0399 us | 9.3074 us | 1.6159x | 5.7325 us |
| 2 | 15.0453 us | 9.2894 us | 1.6196x | 5.7559 us |
| Pooled | 15.0425 us | 9.2989 us | 1.6177x | 5.7437 us |

Both processes loaded kernel SHA256 `a533ddd9a728258c...`, wrapper SHA256
`0d8a237ee3bcda204...`, and compiled code-object SHA256
`4a711d6dfb964325...`. Same-input graph replay was bitwise stable and a changed
input changed the output.

A historical minimal TP8 reconstruction used an 8,192-token input and
1,024-token output, TP8, FP8 KV cache, `max_num_seqs=128`, and no speculative
decoding. It is retained as supporting evidence; the current accepted-stack
kernel-only pair below is the primary endpoint attribution.

| Stack | Median decode | Range | Median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Reproduced historical parent (#4405 + closed vLLM #50054) | 45.9329 tok/s | 45.8805-45.9823 | 21.7709 ms |
| Parent + group64 | 46.8310 tok/s | 46.7372-46.9210 | 21.3534 ms |

Across three trials the candidate gains 0.8981 tok/s (1.9552%) and removes
0.4175 ms/token; the ranges do not overlap. The endpoint images differed only
by the companion AITER and vLLM KDA changes and carried exact source-SHA
labels. AITER #4405 and vLLM #50054 were present identically in both images.

The kernel-only endpoint comparison uses the immutable accepted Kimi-K3 stack
and changes exactly this PR's FlyDSL kernel and wrapper. Both endpoints use the
same TP8, FP8-KV, no-speculation, B1 8K-input/1K-output contract.

| Kernel | Median decode | Range | Median TPOT |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Accepted 8-element/1-row | 75.8497 tok/s | 75.7827-76.3786 | 13.1840 ms |
| Current 16-element/2-row | 76.7216 tok/s | 76.5235-76.8229 | 13.0341 ms |

Across three trials per stack, the current kernel adds 0.8718 tok/s (1.1494%)
and removes 0.1498 ms/token; the ranges do not overlap. The fixed GSM8K
first-100 gate passes at 99/100 with zero invalid responses, versus the exact
old image's frozen 100/100 result. Both use prompt SHA256 `633f7a17...` and
evaluator SHA256 `867c3583...`; the candidate's only miss is question 84.

The minimal current-upstream integration stack has a separate common model
regression: both its parent and candidate generate runaway answers, including
with BF16 KV. It is not used as accuracy evidence for this kernel PR. The
accepted-stack test above binds the exact current kernel and wrapper hashes and
provides the model-level accuracy gate.

## Validation

```text
ruff check <changed Python files>
ruff format --check <changed Python files>
git diff --check 3a79aec3b71393a36351e2d0512414d9a1ba7813...HEAD
```

All passed. The runtime-source manifest and compiled symbol were verified by
the benchmark harness.

## Prior art and overlap

AITER already provides `wvSplitKQ` and group64 quantization in other attention
compression paths, but no production operator implements this fixed Kimi-K3
KDA projection contract. vllm-project/vllm#50592 changes KDA output ownership;
it does not replace the input projection. The final pre-publication audit covered the current
100 open and 100 most recently updated closed ROCm/AITER pull requests. It
found Kimi-K3 work in MLA, MoE, and serving correctness, but no duplicate KDA
group64 input-projection operator.

## Disclosure

This change was developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. Every changed
line, test, numerical threshold, and benchmark result was reviewed by the
author.

items.title: perf(flydsl): fuse Kimi-K3 MLA output gate on gfx950
items.body:
## Summary

Add a narrowly dispatched gfx950 BF16 kernel for the Kimi-K3 full-MLA output
gate. It fuses the fixed gate projection, production BF16 rounding, stable
sigmoid, and attention multiplication into one FlyDSL launch.

Unsupported inputs raise `NotImplementedError`; the framework callsite retains
ownership of its tuned-GEMM plus elementwise fallback. Generic MLA kernels and
split policy are unchanged.

## Correctness

Two independent processes covered 36 cases each. The worst relative RMSE
against the FP32 oracle was 0.003051, minimum cosine similarity was 0.9999954,
and minimum finite SNR was 50.31 dB. Coverage includes graph replay with
changed inputs, mutation checks, output reuse/in-place aliasing, the dispatch
predicate, unsupported shapes, and invalid output buffers.

The clean sources also pass all eight focused AITER tests when mounted over the
accepted runtime image.

## Performance

Measured on gfx950 with 100 operations per graph, 100,000 warmup operations, 21
trials, two independent processes, and 13 rotating weights (286.26 MB):

| Boundary | Incumbent P1/P2 p50 | Candidate P1/P2 p50 | Mean speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Gate projection + sigmoid x attention | 12.6345 / 12.6313 us | 5.4140 / 5.4980 us | **2.315x** |

The candidate replaces three launches with one. In the TP8 B1 8K/1K
no-speculative-decoding endpoint, the combined AITER/vLLM integration improves
the exact FP8-KV parent from 72.6625 to 73.9572 tok/s/GPU (13.7623 to 13.5213
ms TPOT). Native Torch profiling attributes a 0.231 ms critical-path reduction
and 48 fewer launches per token.

## Validation

- AITER focused tests: 8/8 passed on gfx950.
- Combined AITER/vLLM mounted-source tests: 11/11 passed.
- Current Ruff check/format, Black, Python compilation, and `git diff --check`
  pass on the clean current-main diff.
- CUDA-graph TP8 endpoint: two stable repeats passed.
- Paired GSM8K first 100: 99/100 versus 100/100 reference, zero invalid,
  accepted at the frozen 1% floor.
- No overlapping open Kimi-K3 MLA-gate PR was found in ROCm/aiter at rebuild
  time.

ROCm/aiter#4480 and vllm-project/vllm#50563 change FP8-KV decode before this
post-attention gate and are compatible. This PR does not change MLA split
selection or KV-cache precision.

The vLLM AMD-only callsite integration is a separate PR. No NVIDIA dispatch or
generic MLA policy is changed here.

## Disclosure

Developed with assistance from OpenAI Codex. The author reviewed the precision
boundary, kernel schedule, graph behavior, tests, and performance evidence.

items.title: Refactor speech engines behind backend contract
items.body:
## Что изменено

- Вынесены backend-neutral contracts для speech engines:
  - runtime paths;
  - child-process environment;
  - renderer/master command builders;
  - synthesis session/audio spec;
  - production capability gate.
- VoxCPM2-specific loading, KV-cache setup и `model.generate()` mapping находятся в `services/speech_backends/voxcpm2.py`.
- Generic direct/project/Gemini/custom runtime вызывают `_run_speech_and_master()` и не собирают VoxCPM-specific commands/env сами.
- `request.json` получает canonical `speech_backend`; неизвестные или непригодные backend-ы отклоняются до queueing/preflight.
- Сохранены semantic blocks, continuation, pronunciation/stress QA, checkpoints, source-prosody diagnostic-only и final media QA.
- Добавлены contract/request/capability tests и документы по backend boundary.

MOSS-TTS v1.5-specific inference code намеренно не добавлялся в этот PR, чтобы не конфликтовать с отдельным агентом. После его adapter-а orchestration менять не потребуется.

## Проверки

- `python -m compileall -q services handlers tools tests`
- `ruff check --exclude .venv .`
- `git diff --check`
- focused CI smoke: `64 passed`
- engine/capability backend tests: `22 passed`
- `v68_quality_contract=True`

Полный historical pytest не объявляется зелёным: в checkout остаются старые несовместимые ожидания v4/v5 и отдельные runtime/environment-dependent tests.

## Ограничения

- Реальный MOSS/VoxCPM model render и MP4 в Linux sandbox не запускались.
- Workflow-файл оставлен в состоянии `origin/main`, потому что GitHub App не имел `workflows` permission для его изменения. Новые проверки выполнены локально.

items.title: fix: audit findings #1263 #1276 #1278 — heap OOB, vision_server race, SSRF
items.body:
### **User description** Three verified audit findings, all in the vision_server / generic-backend stack: - #1263 HIGH — backend_generic CPU attention sized `scores` to head_dim but indexed by past position; prompts >128 tokens wrote past the heap. Verified with a 202-token prompt before/after. - #1276 HIGH — vision_server shared one Backend* across httplib's thread pool with no lock; the handler now runs under g_inference_mutex. - #1278 MED — vl_download_image SSRF guard was hostname prefix matching (bypassable: nip.io, decimal literals, userinfo); now resolves and rejects private/loopback/link-local addresses, fails closed on unresolved hosts. Verified all bypass forms blocked, external fetch still works. ___ ### **PR Type** Bug fix, Security, Enhancement ___ ### **Description** - Fix heap OOB in generic backend attention scores sizing - Add mutex to serialize vision_server backend access - Harden SSRF guard with address resolution and blocking - Fail closed on unresolvable hosts in image downloads ___ ### Diagram Walkthrough ```mermaid flowchart LR A["backend_generic.cpp"] -- "scores sized to max_seq_len" --> B["Fix heap OOB"] C["vision_server.cpp"] -- "add g_inference_mutex" --> D["Serialize backend access"] E["vl_processor.cpp"] -- "resolve & block private IPs" --> F["Harden SSRF guard"] ```

File Walkthrough
Relevant files
Bug fix
backend_generic.cpp
Fix scores vector size for attention                                         
src/backend_generic.cpp
  • Resize scores vector to max_seq_len instead of head_dim
  • Prevent heap out-of-bounds writes for long prompts
  • Add comment explaining the fix for issue #1263
 +4/-1     
vision_server.cpp
Add mutex for backend concurrency safety                                 
tools/vision_server.cpp
  • Add global mutex to serialize backend access
  • Wrap chat completions handler with lock_guard
  • Prevent concurrent KV-cache corruption from thread pool
 +3/-0     
Security
vl_processor.cpp
Harden SSRF guard with address resolution                               
src/vl_processor.cpp
  • Replace hostname prefix matching with getaddrinfo resolution
  • Block private, loopback, and link-local addresses (IPv4/IPv6)
  • Fail closed on unresolvable hosts to prevent SSRF
  • Strip port and IPv6 brackets before resolution

- ggml-sycl: fix F16 cache + MKL FA multi-turn corruption; add gate guards

Two changes:

1. Always copy F16 K/V to dense row-major buffers before MKL GEMM.
   Previously F16 was read in-place with raw tensor strides. During
   multi-turn conversations, the accumulated KV cache had different
   stride properties than a fresh prefill, producing corrupted outputs.
   Now dense F16 gets a fast memcpy; interleaved (Gemma) gets a strided
   copy kernel. This matches what the quantized paths already did through
   to\_fp16\_sycl.

2. Gate MKL FA on unsupported op params (max\_bias, logit\_softcap, batch
   dim mismatch) and pathological F16 strides (nb\[1] not a multiple of
   ne\[0]\*2). These conditions would previously crash inside the MKL
   kernel. Pathological strides (test-only) and ALiBi/softcap fall
   through to TILE/VEC which handle them correctly.

The stride check uses modulo rather than equality, so both dense
(nb1 == ne0*2) and interleaved (nb1 == H \* ne0*2) pass — all real
models use these layouts. Only test cases with overlapping rows
(nb1=32 or nb1=75 for ne0=40) are blocked.

Thanks to hmscider for the oneDNN FA PR ([#​25222](https://redirect.github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25222)) which surfaced the
same insight: always normalize inputs to contiguous F16 before GEMM.

items.title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T quality degrades with sequence length — PPL 384 vs Llama-3.2-1B's 16.3, generation collapses
items.body:
## Summary

BitNet b1.58 2B4T output quality in dotLLM **degrades with sequence length**. Perplexity is ~23x worse than a Llama-3.2-1B measured with identical methodology on identical tokens, and long greedy generation collapses into a repetition loop where Llama does not.

Root cause **not yet identified**. Several candidates have been eliminated (below). Filing with the evidence and the eliminations so the next person does not repeat them.

**This is invisible to every existing BitNet gate**, which is the reason it shipped: all of them use short prompts and/or greedy argmax, and argmax survives any monotonic distortion of the logits.

## Evidence

### 1. Perplexity, wikitext-2, CPU

| model | teacher-forced ctx=512 | sliding-window (llama.cpp methodology) |
|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.2-1B-Q8_0 | 12.11 | **16.30** |
| BitNet-b1.58-2B-4T | 176.69 | **384.40** |

BitNet is 23.6x worse on the standard methodology (4,080 scored tokens, +/- 18.3 — the error bar is tight). Microsoft reports this model as on par with full-precision peers of similar size, which for a 2B model means roughly 9-13, not 384.

### 2. The degradation scales with context

Teacher-forced, same corpus, same method. The **ratio to a healthy model** is the controlled signal, since both score identical nested token sets:

| ctx | BitNet | Llama-3.2-1B | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | 219.7 | 170.1 | 1.29 |
| 32 | 136.1 | 125.8 | 1.08 |
| 64 | 62.6 | 41.2 | 1.52 |
| 128 | 50.4 | 18.9 | 2.66 |
| 256 | 116.2 | 17.9 | **6.50** |

Llama improves monotonically with context, as expected. BitNet improves to ctx=128 then **reverses**. Finer sampling shows a smooth ramp rather than a cliff — 128: 50.4, 144: 51.3, 160: 66.6, 192: 94.0, 224: 120.2 — so the per-token error grows with position rather than a buffer tipping over at a fixed size.

### 3. Long generation degenerates (with control)

Identical settings, greedy (`--temp 0`), 220 tokens, same prompt:

- **BitNet**: coherent for ~40 tokens, then "The Roman Empire was one of the most powerful empires in the world." repeated, then "Rome. Rome.", then an unbounded loop of "that was the world's largest empire that was the world's largest empire...".
- **Llama-3.2-1B** (control): a coherent, well-structured paragraph that terminates naturally.

The control matters: greedy decoding produces repetition loops in healthy models too, so BitNet's collapse is only meaningful next to a model that does not collapse under the same settings.

## Eliminated

- **Backend-specific bug.** All four backends agree to 0.19% (CPU 176.69, Vulkan-Arc 176.36, Vulkan-NVIDIA 176.37, CUDA 176.36). The CPU forward is the golden reference the GPU paths are parity-gated against, so a CPU-side defect propagates everywhere and this agreement is expected rather than reassuring.
- **Tokenization.** BitNet and Llama-3.2-1B produce **byte-identical token ids** for the same corpus (same Llama-3 tokenizer). Verified with `--dump-tokens`.
- **BOS.** `--bos` changes the result to 7 significant figures, i.e. not at all. (Separately worth checking whether `--bos` is actually applied in teacher-forced mode.)
- **RoPE configuration.** Extracted config matches the GGUF exactly: theta 500000, dimension_count 128, scaling None, Norm pairing (BitNet is Llama-shaped, so Norm is correct).
- **KV cache.** Teacher-forced growing-prefix issues a fresh full forward per prefix with no cache, so the degradation reproduces with the cache entirely out of the picture.
- **Sub-LN axis.** Both BitNet Sub-LN sites (`AttnSubNormWeight` before o_proj, `FfnSubNormWeight` before ffn_down) apply `RmsNorm` per token over the hidden dim, not across the sequence. Correct.
- **Activation quantisation granularity.** `QuantizeInput` is per token; and the CPU BitNet path is W2A16 (F32 activations), so activation quant is not in the loop at all.

## Remaining candidates

- Attention masking or scaling in the multi-token prefill path specifically.
- Error accumulation in the I2_S quantized matmul that scales with sequence length.
- The ReLU^2 / gated activation path.
- Something genuinely model-side (an instruct-tuned model can score worse on raw text) — but not by 23x, and that would not explain the *context-dependence* or the generation collapse.

## Why the existing gates miss it

This is the part worth fixing regardless of the root cause:

- `BitNetVulkanAccuracyTests` compares CPU vs GPU. A CPU-side defect is invisible to it by construction.
- `BitNetReferenceParityTests` compares **greedy decode** against Microsoft's bitnet.cpp on 5 short probes. Argmax is preserved under any monotonic distortion of the distribution, so this cannot detect a calibration error — and 5 short probes cannot detect a length-dependent one.
- `BitNetAccuracyTests` records a CPU perplexity of 15.21, but on a short fixed passage, i.e. below the context length where the degradation appears.

Suggested gate: a perplexity check against a **reference NLL** (not argmax) at a context length of at least 512. The harness now supports this (`dotllm perplexity --device cpu|cuda|vulkan`).

## Reproduction

```
dotllm perplexity <bitnet-gguf> -f wikitext2-test.raw --device cpu --context 512
dotllm perplexity <llama-3.2-1b-gguf> -f wikitext2-test.raw --device cpu --context 512
```

Corpus: wikitext-2 raw test split, obtainable from
`https://huggingface.co/datasets/Salesforce/wikitext/resolve/main/wikitext-2-raw-v1/test-00000-of-00001.parquet`
(join the `text` column with newlines).

items.title: chore(#2929): generalize prompt-budget into the shared context-composer seam
items.body: ## Feature PR ## Linked Issue Closes #2929 Phase 2 of epic #1671 (Dynamic Context Management). Design lock: [ADR-1671](../blob/next/docs/adr/1671-dynamic-context-management-platform.md) Decision item 2 + "Architecture and contracts", migration step 3. --- ## Feature summary `prompt-budget.applyBudget()` already did priority-ordered, budget-trimmed composition, but it was walled inside the cross-AI review pipeline, so per-runtime emission had no trimming primitive to call. This lifts that logic into a shared `context-composer` seam with an injectable budget unit, leaving `prompt-budget` as a caller whose output is byte-for-byte unchanged. ## What changed ### New files | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `src/context-composer.cts` | The shared seam. `composeWithinBudget()` trims an ordered fragment list to a measured budget and returns a **plan** of surviving fragments — never rendered text. Also exports the `headShrink`/`tailTruncate` primitives, previously private to `prompt-budget`. | | `scripts/gen-prompt-budget-parity-corpus.cjs` | `--write`/`--check` generator for the characterization corpus. `--check` is a drift-guard: a diff means review-prompt output moved. | | `tests/fixtures/prompt-budget-parity/corpus.json` | 50 cases captured from the **pre-refactor** implementation. The phase's success oracle. | | `tests/prompt-budget-parity.test.cjs` | Replays every corpus case and asserts byte-identical `prompt` + field-identical `metadata`. | | `tests/context-composer.test.cjs` | Unit tests for the new seam, `flexReserve`, and `isolate`. | | `tests/context-composer.property.test.cjs` | Five `fast-check` invariants, including the budget-monotonicity property the issue names. | ### Modified files | File | What changed | |------|-------------| | `src/prompt-budget.cts` | 436 → 343 lines. `applyBudget` keeps its exact signature, metadata shape and both hard-fail paths, and now builds a fragment list and delegates. Its private `headShrink`/`tailTruncate` moved to the composer. `estimateTokens` deliberately stays and is unchanged. | | `docs/adr/1671-…md` | Composer contract amended — see Implementation notes. | | `CONTEXT.md` | New `### Context Composer Module` glossary entry (PR gate for new domain modules). | | `docs/INVENTORY.md`, `docs/INVENTORY-MANIFEST.json` | New CLI-module row. | | `scripts/mutation-matrix.cjs` | `context-composer` entry at the same floor as `prompt-budget`. | | `scripts/lint-test-file-count.allowlist.json` | `prompt-budget` entry — see below. | | `.gitignore` | `context-composer.cjs` tsc output. | ## Implementation notes **ADR-1671's stated composer mechanism could not reproduce the function it generalizes, and the ADR is amended in this PR to say so.** The ADR specified "priority + binary-search cutoff to a per-runtime budget". Read against the code, `applyBudget` is not a cutoff at all — it is a fixed five-step ladder in which each section carries its own *shrink strategy*, and only three of its eight sections are ever dropped: | # | Section | Strategy | Droppable? | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `instructions` | verbatim | never | | 2 | note | injected only under pressure, reserving 80 tokens | n/a | | 3 | `roadmap` | verbatim | never | | 4 | `projectMd` | **head-shrink** to N lines | never dropped, only shrunk | | 5 | `plans` | **proportional tail-truncate, per-plan 1024-byte floor** | never dropped | | 6–8 | `context`, `research`, `requirements` | drop, in that order | yes | A cutoff composer sorts by priority and discards the tail. It cannot express "head-shrink this one", "truncate that one but never below its floor", or "these three are the only droppables, in this order". Building to the literal contract and routing `prompt-budget` through it would have **silently changed review-prompt output** — the one outcome this phase forbids. So shrink strategies are the core abstraction and binary-search cutoff becomes one strategy among them, for per-runtime emission in Phases 3–4. Three further decisions: - **The composer decides; the caller renders.** It returns a fragment plan, never a string. `assemblePrompt`'s rendering is prompt-shaped; owning it in the composer would force emission to adopt prompt-shaped rendering. The split is what lets one seam serve both consumers. - **The budget unit is injected** via `measure(text)`. The old code converted tokens to characters with a hardcoded `* 4`; that is now an explicit `charsPerUnit` inverse, which is exactly what a byte unit needs to reuse this. - **Entry point is `composeWithinBudget`, not `applyBudget`.** That name already exists twice (`src/prompt-budget.cts`, `src/graphify.cts` — an unrelated graph-edge budget). It already misresolves: Memtrace `preflight_check`/`get_impact` for "applyBudget" return graphify's. **On the test-file allowlist entry:** the parity suite makes `prompt-budget` a three-file module. Consolidating it into `prompt-budget.test.cjs` is the wrong fix — it is generated rather than hand-written, is its own mutation-scoring target, and its failure means something categorically different from a unit failure: not "this behavior is wrong" but "observable output moved". The allowlist is an identity ratchet, so the entry pins today's three filenames; a fourth still fails. ## Spec compliance - [x] `context-composer` seam exists in `src/`, compiles to `gsd-core/bin/lib/` - [x] `prompt-budget` delegates to it with **no** change to its existing output (parity assertion test) — 50/50 byte-identical - [x] Boundary tests at `cap-1` / `cap` / `cap+1` - [x] ≥1 `fast-check` property test (budget monotonicity: more budget never yields less content) - [x] `flexReserve` floors honored — a floored fragment is never trimmed - [x] Byte-stable canonical prefix preserved across runtimes - [x] `prompt-budget` Stryker floor still met — `context-composer` added to the matrix at the same floor so the relocated ladder is measured rather than silently unscored *(CI-verified)* - [x] Remote matrix green; `npm run lint:ci` clean ## Testing ### Test coverage **The corpus is validated by mutation, not trusted because it is green.** Seven defects were injected into the composer; every one is caught, and the unmutated build returns 0/50: | Injected defect | Cases that catch it | |---|---| | note reserve deducted unconditionally instead of only under pressure | 4 | | pressure test relaxed from `>` to `>=` | 1 | | no-op head-shrink still sets its flag | 1 | | per-fragment floor ignored in proportional-truncate | 1 | | drop order reversed | 1 | | `Math.floor` → `Math.round` on `effectiveBudget` | 1 | | `Math.floor` → `Math.ceil` on `effectiveBudget` | 3 | Two of those exposed real holes in the first cut of the corpus and are why several cases exist at all: - **`>=` was caught by nothing.** At exact cap the only trimmable fragment was a floored plan group, and the 1024-char floor absorbed the whole trim, so the mutation was byte-invisible. `A3b`/`A3c` put a droppable at exactly the cap, making the strict inequality observable. - **Nothing reached `proportional-truncate` at all** — `B6`/`B7` both hard-failed the min-set pre-check first, so `planTruncationPct` was 0 across every case and the floor semantics were unexercised. Rebudgeted so the step is actually reached. - **The rounding mode was unpinned** (found by an isolated reviewer): every budget/margin pair produced a whole number. `A11`–`A13` straddle `.5`. Boundary coverage follows `RULESET.TESTS.boundary-coverage.fixtures`, including row (d) — the reserve band. `CONTEXT.md`'s `LEARNING.prompt-budget.boundary-gap` records PR #3708 shipping two regressions that only fired when the baseline sat inside that band, because the suite paired a trivially-fitting budget with a trivially-overflowing one and never sampled between. `A4` sweeps from the cap down to 81 tokens under it and pins that nothing is trimmed; `A10` mirrors it above the cap. ### Platforms tested - [x] macOS - [x] Windows (including backslash path handling) - [x] Linux Full `(OS × Node)` matrix via the remote runner on the exact HEAD sha. The changed code is pure string/number logic with no path handling. ### Runtimes tested - [x] N/A — `prompt-budget` is invoked through `gsd_run query prompt-budget`, which is runtime-agnostic. No runtime-specific surface is touched. --- ## Scope confirmation - [x] The implementation matches the scope approved in the linked issue exactly - [x] No additional features, commands, or behaviors were added beyond what was approved - [x] If scope changed during implementation, I updated the issue spec and received re-approval The ADR contract amendment is recorded in `docs/adr/1671-…md` in this PR rather than changing the issue's scope: the deliverable is unchanged, only the mechanism that can satisfy it. ## Documentation - [x] Updated the relevant file(s) under `docs/` to reflect this feature — `docs/adr/1671-…md` (architectural), `docs/INVENTORY.md` + manifest, plus the `CONTEXT.md` glossary entry - [x] All `docs/` content added in this PR is written in English - [ ] N/A — docs were updated, so no exemption is claimed ## Checklist - [x] Issue linked above with `Closes #2929` - [x] Linked issue has the `approved-feature` label - [x] All acceptance criteria from the issue are met (listed above) - [x] Implementation scope matches the approved spec exactly - [x] All existing tests pass - [x] New tests cover the happy path, error cases, and edge cases - [x] `.changeset/` fragment added - [x] No unnecessary external dependencies added — the seam is pure, with no imports beyond the repo - [x] Works on Windows (backslash paths handled) — no path handling in the changed code ## Breaking changes None. `applyBudget` keeps its exact exported signature, its `BudgetResult`/`BudgetMetadata` shapes, and both hard-fail paths; all 50 characterization cases reproduce byte-identically. `estimateTokens` deliberately stays in `prompt-budget` with unchanged math — `src/phase-estimation.cts` re-exports it as `measureTokens`, and `CONTEXT.md` pins plan estimates and recorded actuals to that same scale, so moving or changing it would silently break the calibration loop. ## Known limits (disclosed) 1. **No emission consumer lands in this phase.** The byte-unit capability, `flexReserve` and `isolate` are unwired until Phases 3–4. An unwired export is normally a defect; here it is ADR-1671's stated sequencing, and the alternative is designing the seam twice. An isolated reviewer correctly flagged the net LOC growth (436 → 654 across two files for one consumer) as speculative generality — accurate, and the justification is the sequencing, not a claim that it is already simpler. What did fall is internal complexity: `prompt-budget` went 436 → 343 lines and from eighteen mutable accumulators to two, both inside a verbatim-copied helper. 2. **``'s test can only assert byte-stability, not KV-cache benefit** — there is no cross-runtime consumer yet. 3. **Parity is proven for the review ladder only.** The composer accepts strategy combinations no current caller exercises; those are covered by unit and property tests, not by a real-caller corpus. 4. **`estimateTokens` remains chars/4.** Not a real tokenizer, and unchanged here — which is precisely why the ADR's emission budget unit is bytes. --- Need help on this PR? items.title: feat(server): images over /v1/chat/completions for Qwen3-VL
items.body:
The CLI route shipped in #1178; this is the HTTP one. Same split the mmproj path already uses — CPU preprocessing on the request thread, GPU encode on the batch worker — but **per-request throughout**, because the server admits image requests concurrently.

```
HTTP thread  : decode + smart_resize + patchify -> QwenPatches on the request.
               The token count is known HERE, which is what lets the prompt
               reserve exactly that many placeholders before tokenizing.
batch worker : patches -> this request's own embedding and DeepStack buffers,
               its own (t, h, w) layout, its own decode offset.
```

## Verification

Against the staged `Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`, a cat photo and a pizza photo:

- sequentially, **in both orders**, repeatedly — each described correctly;
- **four concurrent image requests plus one text request** — all correct, and the concurrent answers are **byte-identical** to the sequential ones.

## Three bugs this found, in order of severity

### 1. The prefix cache was serving one request's picture to another

It is content-addressed on **token ids**, and every image token carries the **same** id (`<|image_pad|>`, or the soft token on the mmproj path). Two requests with different pictures therefore share a long identical prefix, and the second one answered about the first one's image:

> **Q:** *(pizza photo)* "What food is this?"
> **A:** "Actually, this is not food—it's a **cat**. The image shows a tabby cat sitting outdoors…"

Image requests now neither **read from** nor **publish to** the cache. Publishing is as unsound as reading: a later *text* prompt sharing the prefix would inherit a picture's KV.

**This was a pre-existing bug on the mmproj path**, not something the new code introduced — the ids are just as uniform there.

There are **two** reuse sites — `engine_scheduler.cpp` and `scheduler.cpp`. Guarding one and testing only through the CLI would have looked exactly like a fix; the second one is what the server actually uses.

### 2. The decode position offset was engine-global

Decode replays dereference that pointer *at replay time*, so a concurrent request's prefill overwrote the value another sequence was mid-generation on. Symptom: `"ThisThisThisThis…"`. It lives on the `Request` now.

### 3. The two decode paths computed the offset from different sources

The batched path used host `context_len()`; the single-sequence path used device `positions`. They agree until a captured graph runs ahead of the host — then a single token comes out wrong (`"a domestic shorth brown"`). Both now add a **per-token** offset to the same device positions.

## Known cost

An image request cannot use the prefix cache **at all**, so a multi-turn conversation about one picture re-prefills it every turn. The right fix is to fold an image content hash into the block hash rather than skip the cache — that is a KV-manager change and does not belong here.

## Regression

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| test-core / compute / attention / kv / quant / text / moe-gdn / e2e | all green |
| `degen_suite.py` vs served Qwen3-4B-Q8 | 34 checks, 0 FAIL |
| Text prefix caching still active | second identical text prompt reports `cached_tokens: 400` |
| File size / alloc sites | clean |

items.title: EXL3: one-grid mixed K3/K4 regresses large-M SM120 prefill
items.body:
## Summary

The one-grid mixed K3/K4 Trellis path from #104 is faster for small-M decode, but it regresses large-M GLM-5.2 prefill on SM120 because the mixed launch currently uses route block 8 while the actual predecessor used two serial homogeneous-tier launches with route block 64.

This was first visible as an approximately 23% full-server prefill regression between the published r13 and r14 images. A controlled r14 hybrid that retained every other r14 component and changed only this executor geometry recovered the loss.

## Corrected kernel comparison

The existing mixed-Trellis benchmark's serial control uses the mixed tile and block 8. That does not represent the deployed r13 predecessor, which used serial tile `(64, 256, 64, 256)` and block 64 for prefill.

On one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.2), after correcting the control:

| Active rows | Serial homogeneous tiers, block 64 | Mixed one-grid, block 8 | Serial speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 689.22 us | 1,212.00 us | 1.76x |
| 2,048 | 1,917.54 us | 4,636.96 us | 2.42x |
| 3,072 | 2,815.07 us | 8,732.74 us | 3.10x |

At equal block 8, the one-grid path is 1.65x faster at 32 rows and 1.03x faster at 3,072 rows. This is useful for decode, but it obscures the prefill regression when the predecessor's block-64 geometry is omitted.

Trying route block 64 on the mixed path does not currently compile on SM120: the register-count table has no specialization for `(256, 4, 8, 8, False)`.

## Full-server confirmation

Matched GLM-5.2 arms used the same 3.25-bpw checkpoint, TP4/DCP4, MTP5, 524,288 active KV tokens, 2,048 batched tokens, 8 sequences, dynamic NVFP4 MLA KV, CKV gather 140,000, fresh compile/cache namespaces, and the complete r14 stack.

| Prompt | Pristine r14 | Shape-aware r14 | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3,072 | 1,772.9 tok/s | 2,283.2 tok/s | +28.78% |
| 32,768 | 1,660.2 tok/s | 2,146.6 tok/s | +29.30% |
| 131,072 | 1,583.1 tok/s | 2,033.1 tok/s | +28.43% |

The shape-aware build retains one-grid/block-8 for rows up to the decode capture limit and uses shared-arena serial/block-64 tier plans above it. It is within 1.2-1.7% of the r13 server control at all three depths. The 35-request matrix completed with no errors or preemptions, and a 509,022-token prompt retrieved all needles at 10/50/90% depth without degeneration.

## Requested follow-up

1. Add the actual serial/block-64 predecessor to the mixed-path A/B benchmark.
2. Add and tune an SM120 mixed large-block specialization, if feasible.
3. Until that is competitive, keep the one-grid route for decode and use serial homogeneous tiers for prefill.
4. Gate future mixed-path promotion on full-server 3K/32K/128K prefill as well as per-layer and decode results.

I am opening the corresponding vLLM dispatcher/weight-sharing implementation and will cross-link it here.

items.title: Edge Detector: devig the Vegas line, wire /edge/detect, cache odds calls
items.body:
The odds key is live (MLB 0 → 28 games). Three fixes so the Edge Detector is correct, complete, and credit-safe.

## 1. Devig (correctness)
Edge was `polymarket_price − raw_implied_prob`, but raw American-odds probs include the vig and sum to >100% (e.g. 29% + 74% = 103%) — inflating apparent edge on **both** sides and manufacturing false value bets. Now normalized to **no-vig** probabilities before the comparison. Extracted the Vegas↔Polymarket logic into `buildOddsComparison()` so `/odds/compare-all` and the new `/edge/detect` share one correct implementation.

## 2. `/edge/detect/{sport}` (the missing endpoint)
The Edge Detector page called this — it never existed (ungrafted v18 engine). Added as a thin adapter over `buildOddsComparison`, shaped to the page's contract (`dataSources` / `summary` / `topEdges` / `allGames`) with `edgeScore`, confidence tiers, and a plain-English recommendation. **No frontend change needed** — the page already targets this path.

## 3. Credit protection (your 500 free)
`getGameOdds` and `getGameScores` were **uncached** — every call burned Odds API credits (charged per market per region). Added `cachedOddsFetch` KV caching (odds 15 min, scores 30 min), so sustained use stays within the free tier during validation.

Honest scope note: `dataSources` reports `sharpLines: false` / `bettingSplits: false` — this build compares Vegas consensus vs Polymarket only; Pinnacle/betting-splits signals from v18 aren't wired (no data source for them yet).
